cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to Titus, his true child in the faith. Paul left Titus on the island of Crete to set things in order and appoint elders in every town. And there are people in Crete teaching things they should not, so Titus has his hands FULL.

cards.question: With those teachers running around Crete, what does Paul tell Titus to speak?

answers.text: Things the crowds want to hear
Things the town elders voted on

cards.text: Now Paul goes down the line like a coach at halftime, one player at a time. First up, the older men: temperate, dignified, self-controlled, and sound in faith, love, and perseverance.
The older women are next. Paul wants them reverent in their behavior, not slanderers and not addicted to much wine.

cards.question: Paul doesn't only tell the older women what NOT to be. He wants them to be teachers of ___.

cards.text: And here's who they teach. They can train the young women to love their husbands and children, and to be self-controlled, pure, kind, managers of their households, and submissive to their own husbands.

cards.question: Paul gives a reason for how the young women should live. What is it?

answers.text: So the word of God won't be discredited
So the church in Crete will grow larger
So their households will be admired in town

cards.question: Paul's word for the younger men is short. Titus is to urge them to be ___.

cards.text: Then Paul turns to Titus himself. Friend, I once handed out jobs in the bakery, found my OWN name at the bottom of the list, and washed every bowl in the place.

cards.question: Paul doesn't want Titus teaching with words alone. What else is Titus to show them?

answers.text: Himself as an example of good works
A scroll of rules for every town
Letters from Paul to every church

cards.question: Paul says Titus only needs to be an example in the big things.

cards.text: In his teaching, Titus is to show integrity, dignity, and wholesome speech that is above reproach. Clean every time, not blurry like my stamps back when my edges were worn down.

cards.question: Paul says that if Titus teaches this way, the people who oppose them will have plenty of bad things to say about them.

cards.text: Next, Paul speaks to slaves. They are to submit to their own masters in everything, be well-pleasing, and not be argumentative.

cards.question: Instead of stealing from their masters, slaves are to show all good ___.

cards.text: Paul gives a reason here too, just like he did for the young women.

cards.question: If slaves live this way, then in every respect they will ___ the teaching about God our Savior.

cards.text: Adorn, like sprinkles on a cookie that's already good, the kind that makes everybody want a bite. Then Paul says, 'For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to everyone.'

cards.question: Paul says the grace of God doesn't only bring salvation. It instructs us too. What does it teach us to renounce?
Grace teaches us to wait until a later age to live sensible, upright and godly lives.

cards.text: Living godly lives right now isn't the whole picture, because Paul says we're waiting too. And friend, this isn't waiting on hold with a phone company. This wait comes with a HOPE.

cards.question: Paul says we await the blessed hope. What appearance are we waiting for?

answers.text: The glorious appearance of Jesus Christ
The appearance of a new prophet
The appearance of a king in Crete

cards.text: Paul calls Jesus 'our great God and Savior Jesus Christ.' Nobody's told me the day, friend, so I keep my ovens HOT.

cards.question: Paul says Jesus gave ___ for us, to redeem us from all lawlessness.

cards.text: Somebody once bought me out of a bakery's clearance bin for 25 cents, and Jesus gave HIMSELF, friend. He did it to purify for Himself a people for His own possession.

cards.question: Jesus purifies a people for His own possession. What does Paul say those people are zealous for?

cards.text: Paul wraps up with one last word for Titus: speak these things, with all authority.

cards.question: Paul tells Titus to encourage people but never to rebuke them.
Titus is to speak with all authority. What does Paul say no one should do to Titus?

findings.problem: The card calls Paul 'an apostle of Jesus Christ,' which comes from Titus 1:1. The card cites only Titus 1:4-11, so its citation starts too late. It should be Titus 1:1-11.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't click. Papa Dorin hands out the jobs himself, so 'found my OWN name at the bottom of the list' makes no sense, and a reader has to work out how this connects to Titus being an example by doing good works (2:7). It needs one clear image with the same core action: leading by doing the work yourself.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: 'Paul speaks to slaves' is not what the text shows. Paul is telling Titus what to teach about slaves (2:1, 2:9, 2:15). He is not addressing slaves directly. The cards about the other groups say this correctly ('older women are next').

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the BSB's wording ('good faith'). 'Good cheer' fits the sentence just as naturally, so a baker can't reason between 'faith' and 'cheer' without having seen the verse.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This card is a single flat setup line with none of Papa Dorin's voice. It reads like a stage direction, not like him.

rule.text: A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card spends its opening words explaining what 'adorn' means ('like sprinkles on a cookie'). Hard words get a dictionary pop-up instead. The card also carries two beats: the explanation of 'adorn' and the start of 2:11.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. It is the only answer with a Bible-sounding word ('glorious') and the only one that names Jesus. The two wrong answers are plain and generic, so the right one is easy to spot.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
